tasks.label: yamt: run the merge window
tasks.detail: Start the merge window (just dev-web), then open http://localhost:5173 in GNOME Web. Running it again restarts it with the current code; an open page reloads itself. Stop it with Ctrl+C in its terminal.

tasks.label: golden: build conflict repo
tasks.detail: Rebuild one of the 10 real conflicts as a git repo in /tmp/yamt-<case>, to open it in WebStorm/PhpStorm.

tasks.label: merge: new conflict project
tasks.detail: Replace /tmp/yamt-conflict-project with the demo project (scripts/demo-repo.sh): Taskboard, a small TypeScript kanban app with oxlint and oxfmt, stopped while main merges feature/reminders. 7 conflicted files: src/board/board.ts (about 450 lines, changes on both sides all through it), card.ts, cardView.ts, client.ts, mockBoards.ts (deleted on one side), docs/shortcuts.md, public/logo.png (an image changed on both sides). The merge causes one TypeScript error in board.ts and leaves one oxlint warning, shown once main's changes there are applied. Installs typescript-language-server once into ~/.cache/yamt (needs the network the first time; scripts/lsp-servers.sh).

tasks.label: merge: open in WebStorm
tasks.detail: Open the demo project /tmp/yamt-conflict-project (scripts/demo-repo.sh: Taskboard mid-merge, 7 conflicted files; made first if missing) in WebStorm; then Git → Resolve Conflicts.

tasks.label: merge: open in yamt
tasks.detail: Build yamt (debug, pages built in) from the current code and open it on the demo project /tmp/yamt-conflict-project (scripts/demo-repo.sh: Taskboard mid-merge, 7 conflicted files; made first if missing), with ~/.cache/yamt/servers-path first on PATH (scripts/lsp-servers.sh --path) so typescript-language-server is found; oxlint and oxfmt come from the project's node_modules. The first time, yamt asks whether to start the project's language servers. Running it again closes the open yamt window and rebuilds. The terminal shows yamt's exit status when you close it.
tasks.command: test -d /tmp/yamt-conflict-project/.git || scripts/demo-repo.sh /tmp/yamt-conflict-project; PATH="$(scripts/lsp-servers.sh --path):$PATH" just app --repo /tmp/yamt-conflict-project; echo "yamt exit status: $?"

tasks.label: lsp: new conflict project
tasks.detail: Replace /tmp/yamt-lsp-project with a fresh repo in the middle of a merge: one project per language (web/ with TypeScript, Vue, oxlint and oxfmt; biome/; py/ with ruff, ty and basedpyright; rs/ for rust-analyzer; go/ for gopls; php/ for Phpactor or Intelephense; c/ for clangd), each with a conflicted file and, outside the conflicts, one problem per server and a badly formatted line; web/src/greet.ts is the one conflicted file with no seeds. Installs the pinned servers once into ~/.cache/yamt (needs the network the first time; scripts/lsp-servers.sh) and prints the PATH line yamt runs with. Your settings file is not touched.

tasks.label: lsp: open in yamt
tasks.detail: Build yamt (debug, pages built in) from the current code and open it on /tmp/yamt-lsp-project (made first if missing), with ~/.cache/yamt/servers-path first on PATH (scripts/lsp-servers.sh --path) so the installed servers are found. The first time, yamt asks whether to start the project's language servers; the answer is kept for that folder (Settings → Language servers changes it). Ctrl+S formats with the project's formatter, then saves. Running it again closes the open yamt window and rebuilds.
tasks.command: test -d /tmp/yamt-lsp-project/.git || scripts/lsp-repo.sh --servers /tmp/yamt-lsp-project; PATH="$(scripts/lsp-servers.sh --path):$PATH" just app --repo /tmp/yamt-lsp-project; echo "yamt exit status: $?"

inputs.description: Real conflict to rebuild in /tmp for PhpStorm
